claims.statement: The application maintains its own usage log as its first-party frequency data source because the machine's `C:\Windows\Prefetch` is empty (prefetching disabled) and UserAssist holds only about four records; the log deliberately stores the process executable path plus a timestamp and never window titles.

`UsageService` owns collection but no timer of its own: both modules of the kernel assembly arm `collect` every `DEFAULT_USAGE_MS` = 2000 ms and `prune` every `USAGE_PRUNE_MS` = 3600 000 ms inside a single `if (usageMs > 0)` branch, so `usageIntervalMs: 0` disables both and tests drive `collect` manually; in production the service is mounted by `createDataplaneKernel` inside the data-plane `utilityProcess` child, which receives the `usageDir` the panel main process resolved.

`detectStarts` diffs the `{pid: exe}` snapshot by pid rather than by executable path, which is what makes a second concurrent instance and an exit-then-restart both count as starts, while a pid whose image path cannot be read never enters the map at all; the first collect round only establishes the pid baseline and emits no start event (though it can still emit one focus event).

Start and focus events are written to separate day-partitioned files (`start-YYYYMMDD.jsonl` / `focus-YYYYMMDD.jsonl`), each record containing exactly `{ts, exe}`; scoring reads only the start stream, so the focus stream is collected but currently unused.

Every event detected in one collect round is stamped with that round's timestamp, so a start's recorded time has the poll interval's resolution (2 s in the service) rather than the OS process creation time.

Day files are named from the event's UTC date and `pruneOldDays` parses the same name back as a UTC day, deleting both kinds of file whose day start falls before `nowMs - RETENTION_DAYS (90) * 86400_000`; pruning runs once in the service constructor and hourly from the kernel timer, and the current day's file can never be deleted because its day start is always inside the window.

The write and read paths are best-effort by construction — `appendEvent` swallows any write failure, `pruneOldDays` swallows the directory read and each failed `unlink`, `readStartEvents` skips unreadable files, malformed lines and future timestamps, `readUserAssistPrior` maps export and parse failures to an empty prior, and the migration records per-file failures instead of throwing — but a collection round itself has no `try`/`catch`, so a throwing source escapes `collect()` into the kernel timer callback, unlike the retired Python run loop that caught per-round exceptions and reported them on a throttle.

The foreground probe resolves only the foreground window's owning process image path (GetForegroundWindow, GetWindowThreadProcessId, OpenProcess with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, QueryFullProcessImageNameW) and never reads window titles; the boundary is enforced by a standing test that scans every `.ts` file under `src/main` recursively for `GetWindowText`/`window_title`, plus a second guard forbidding `SendMessageW` and `title` fields in the focus modules.

The `{ts, exe}` record shape is asserted at two levels of the current suite — on a single `appendEvent` call and on the files a real `UsageService` produced with its process and foreground sources injected — and the live log directory is additionally covered by a behavior-level guard that a full search flow leaves no query text in it.

Frequency is real start count under exponential decay with `HALF_LIFE_DAYS` = 14.0 rather than foreground dwell time; `decay`, `scoreStarts`, `countStarts` and `priorScores` are pure functions that receive `nowMs` as a parameter, so each start contributes an independently decayed weight summed per lowercased executable path and a prior entry folds as `count × decay(age(lastMs))`.

`parseUserAssistEntry` ROT13-decodes the value name, reads the run count as a little-endian u32 at `UA_COUNT_OFFSET` = 4, reads the FILETIME u64 at `UA_FILETIME_OFFSET` = 60, requires at least `UA_MIN_LEN` = 68 bytes and rejects a zero FILETIME; byte offset 0 is a constant 145 session/version field and the offsets must not be "corrected" to 0:4.

The prior read is `reg.exe export` of the UserAssist root key into a temporary file plus a pure text parser: only values under a section whose name ends in `\Count]` are read, `reg`'s folded hex lines are re-joined, ROT13 names are unescaped and decoded, only `.exe`/`.lnk` paths are kept with the largest count per lowercased path winning, GUID subkey names are never hardcoded, and any export or parse failure yields an empty prior; the read is asynchronous so the one-off export never blocks the boot path.

`mapScoresToItems` maps only desktop items with `kind === "shortcut"`: `.exe` paths match a shortcut's resolved target case-insensitively, a resolvable `.lnk` prior entry must match a shortcut's target, and only an unresolvable `.lnk` that does not exist on disk falls back to stem alignment; paths that map to nothing are dropped from the result.

`fuseScores` fuses at the desktop-item level as log score plus `count × decay(age(lastMs)) / (1 + n)`, where n is that item's start count in the self-built log, and drops entries whose fused score is not positive; an empty log (n = 0, weight 1) still yields a non-empty ranking while the prior retires as first-party starts accumulate, and case differences or taskbar `.lnk` priors cannot split or stall an application.

`UsageService.iconScores(items, resolve, exists, nowMs)` composes the cached prior and cached start events through `fuseScores` with no cache of its own result, and the kernel injects it into `DesktopService` as a closure that returns an empty map when the usage service is absent; `DesktopService.computePlan` calls it on every refresh and passes the resulting display-name-keyed map to `planDesktop`.

Frequency scores are consumed only by the app zone's recommended segment, where `scores.get(display) ?? 0` orders the items left after the pinned and explicitly placed segments and a missing score fills a position instead of filtering; document ordering is a separate path that sorts each group by `(-mtimeMs, name)`, because without window titles the log cannot identify which document was in use.

Every detected start is appended to the log, including short-lived tooling and installer processes, while unmappable paths and prior entries for applications absent from the desktop are dropped by `mapScoresToItems` and never appear in a ranking.

Prefetch is not a data source — the prior comes only from the UserAssist registry key, and ADR-0002 records that `C:\Windows\Prefetch` is an empty directory because prefetching is disabled; the Python-era `NoPrefetchTest` source guard was not carried into the TypeScript module, so the boundary now holds by convention rather than by a failing test.

`readStartEvents` skips malformed lines (unparseable JSON, missing `exe`, unparseable `ts`) and ignores events timestamped in the future, so a truncated log or a clock adjustment degrades the ranking instead of failing an arrangement; scoring consumes these events from the service's in-memory cache, which is filled from the day files once per service construction and extended by each round's detected starts.

The live usage log lives at `userData/usage` — `path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'usage')`, resolved by the panel main process and handed to the data-plane child through its init bundle — i.e. machine-written runtime data outside the code tree, matching the documented split from user-edited files; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage` is now only the legacy migration source.

`bootPanel()` runs the usage-log migration after config load and autostart handling and before the kernel (and therefore collection) starts, with `legacyDir: legacyUsageDir()` (the Python-era `%LOCALAPPDATA%\qoder-deck\usage`, which throws when `LOCALAPPDATA` is unset), `targetDir` = `userData/usage` and `markerFile` = `<usageDir>/.legacy-migrated.json`; it is a copy rather than a move, so the legacy directory is left for the user to delete, and the whole call is wrapped so a failure only means the history starts accumulating from zero.

`planUsageMigration` copies only `start-`/`focus-` day files whose UTC day falls inside `RETENTION_DAYS` (90) and skips everything else (non-log files such as `layout.json`, and days that the next rolling cleanup would delete immediately); the plan and `pruneOldDays` derive both the file-name pattern and the cutoff from the same constants and UTC day arithmetic, so migration and retention cannot drift apart.

Migration idempotency rests on a marker file that records migrated file names rather than a single done flag — the pending set is the planned files minus the recorded names, a missing or corrupt marker is treated as "nothing migrated" with the stated bias of re-copying rather than losing history, and if any file fails no marker is written at all so the whole pending set retries on the next boot; the marker lives inside the log directory and matches neither the day-file pattern of `readStartEvents` nor that of `pruneOldDays`.

When a target day file already exists the migration merges instead of overwriting: source lines already present in the target are dropped and only the remainder is appended, which closes the crash window between a successful append and the marker landing on disk; the comparison is against the target's pre-existing lines only, so legitimate duplicate lines inside a source file survive, and because the dedupe is raw line equality any change to `appendEvent`'s serialization changes what counts as a duplicate.

The migration is a byte-preserving file copy rather than a parse-and-rewrite pass, justified by the two sides' record formats being field-identical (`{ts, exe}` JSONL with second-precision ISO timestamps), which removes the opportunity for the old and the new format to drift apart.

`nativeRunningPidExes` returns an empty map when `EnumProcesses` fails, and a round installs whatever it returned as the next baseline, so an enumeration failure makes the following round report every running process as a fresh start; the whole snapshot is bounded by a fixed `MAX_PIDS` = 4096 pid slots.

The cold-start prior is read asynchronously in the service constructor and is not awaited, so the earliest recomputes may run with an empty prior and the recommendation order converges through later recomputes; a rejection is logged as `deck-usage: 冷启动先验读取失败（按无先验继续）` and collection continues without a prior.

In the data-plane child `readShortcutTarget` is a `ProxyShortcutResolver` that answers from a cache, batches misses to the main process and returns `null` for the round that misses (caching the `null` so it is never re-asked), so until those answers land no shortcut item carries a target, no `.exe` log score can resolve to a desktop item, and the recommended segment falls back to name order for the first recomputes.
